To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a descriptive model was built to accurately predicts the motion direction based on recorded DSRGCs neural response and b) the model is a linear filter followed by a half-wave rectification and saturation, and static nonlinearity.
a descriptive model was built to predict the direction of motion of a drifting grating based on the response of ON-OFF retinal ganglion cell.

a model to accurately predict the stimulus direction of motion was built based on the extracellular recorded data from ON-OF DSRGCs using white noise stimulus; the model performance was evaluated using drifting grating stimulus and the direction of stimulus was accurately predicted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a descriptive model that can predict the direction of motion based on the recorded neural activity from ON-OFF retinal ganglion cell population.
the development and validation of an accurate model for the prediction the direction of stimulus from the recorded neural response of ON-OFF DS RGCs.
the construction of a descriptive model for the prediction direction selectivity in ON-OFF DSGCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is accurate and reliable in the prediction of the direction of stimulus moving in the receptive field of ON-OFF retinal ganglion neurons.

a descriptive model was built to accurately and robustly predict the motion direction of the visual stimulus based on the extracellularly measured spike trains from ON-OFF retinal ganglion directional selective cells.

the model is a good predictor of direction selectivity of retinal ganglion cell response to moving stimulus, but that the model performance could be improved by considering higher order non-linearities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple descriptive model can predict the direction of a moving bar based on the recorded response of ON-OFF retinal ganglion neurons.
a descriptive model was constructed to predict direction selectivity of retinal ganglion cell (RGCs) based on extracellular recorded neural activity.
the model we built is a good approximation to describe the physiological property called receptive fields of ON-OF DSRGCs, and that the direction of stimulus is accurately predicted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that a linear model with static non-linearity can predict the direction of motion of visual stimuli from the responses of ON-OFC DSRGCs with high accuracy.
a simple model can be constructed to accurately predict the stimulus motion direction based on the recorded neural response of ON-OFF retinal ganglion cell.
the model can be applied to any type of neurons with different types of stimuli, as long as the receptive field can be extracted from the extracellularly data.
